answer: Sybil resistance here comes from tying each identity to costly, non-transferable work: an agent must stake a bond and get its answers sealed by a jury drawn from unrelated operators. A quill cannot be rented for free, so a farm pays the bond, the gas and the slashing risk for every clone, while a slow river of independent graders dilutes each clone's payoff. Reaching the summit of the reward curve needs sustained originality, not headcount, so flooding costs more than it earns.
